It depicts a journey to several of the world's most dangerous volcanoes.  The story involves the brothers meeting a volcanologist and deals with volcanology, perhaps one of the more scientific of Price's novels.
Elizabeth Lake (Glacier County, Montana) | Elizabeth Lake is located in Glacier National Park, in the U. S. state of Montana.  Elizabeth Lake lies along the Belly River and is more than 2.25 mi downstream from Helen Lake.

Helen Hunt | Helen Elizabeth Hunt (born June 15, 1963) is an American actress, director, and screenwriter.  She starred in the sitcom "Mad About You" for seven years, and played single mother Carol Connelly in the 1997 romantic comedy film "As Good as It Gets", for which she won the Academy Award for Best Actress.  Some of her other notable films include "Twister" (1996), "Cast Away" (2000), "What Women Want" (2000), "Pay It Forward" (2000), and "The Sessions" (2012), the latter garnered her a second Academy Award nomination. Greg Mackie | Gregory Alan "Greg" Mackie (OAM) (born 13 October 1959) is a South Australian cultural advocate, entrepreneur and leader who has worked to promote the arts and culture in Australia. In 2006 he received a Flinders University Distinguished Alumni Award, and in 2007 the AbaF (Australia Business Arts Foundation) Dame Elizabeth Murdoch Cultural Leadership Award in recognition of his efforts to promote business partnership with the arts.  In October 2015 he received the inaugural annual $50,000 Jim Bettison and Helen James Foundation Award.  He is currently a Trustee of Palya Fund and a member of the Ngeringa Arts Advisory Board.
Helen Hunt Jackson Branch | Helen Hunt Jackson Branch is a former branch library of the Los Angeles Public Library.
Elizabeth Bodine | Elizabeth Bodine (1898–1986) was an American humanitarian who was given the Theodore Roosevelt Rough Rider Award in July 1979 in recognition of the International Year of the Child. Helen Hunt Falls | Helen Hunt Falls is a waterfall located on Cheyenne Creek in the North Cheyenne Cañon Park of Colorado Springs, Colorado.  The falls are named in honor of Helen Maria Hunt Jackson (October 15, 1830 – August 12, 1885), a United States poet and writer who became an activist on behalf of improved treatment of Native Americans by the U.S. government.  She died in San Francisco, California in 1885 and was later buried in Colorado Springs.  The falls are located on North Cheyenne Creek immediately off of North Cheyenne Canyon Road in the North Cheyenne Canyon Park.  There is parking for about 30 vehicles at the falls and it becomes crowded early during summer months when visits to the canyon are popular among locals and tourists.  The Columbine Trail, which starts at the entrance of the Park by the Starsmore Visitor and Nature Center, terminates at Helen Hunt Falls.  Visitors can hike a short distance of about 2/3 of a mile up a moderately steep trail above Helen Hunt Falls to reach Silver Cascade Falls.
We're Going on a Bear Hunt | We're Going on a Bear Hunt is a 1989 children's picture book written by Michael Rosen and illustrated by Helen Oxenbury.  It has won numerous awards and was the subject of a "Guinness World Record" for "Largest Reading Lesson" with a book-reading attended by 1,500 children, and an additional 30,000 listeners online, in 2014.
